Marathon Petroleum dropped 5.96% today to $442.57, marking the third consecutive down day after a brief rally on the 26th. The immediate trigger is the sharp fall in oil prices following diplomatic breakthroughs—Iran's supreme leader and top security official discussed conditions to end the war with the U.S. and Israel, and Saudi Arabia's defense minister met with Iran's president to de-escalate tensions. Lower geopolitical risk means lower oil prices (WTI fell to $107.89 from recent highs), and refiners like Marathon profit when oil feedstock is expensive and refined products command premium prices; a retreat from crisis pricing squeezes those margins.

The broader pattern here is whipsaw: for the past week, Middle East tensions were pushing oil higher (Brent hit $116 on the 23rd amid Houthi attacks), lifting refiner stocks on hopes of fatter profit spreads. Now that same region is moving toward de-escalation, reversing that tailwind. U.S. refineries are running at 93.4%, so there's ample capacity to produce if margins allow—but the geopolitical premium that was making crude expensive relative to refined products is now deflating.
